target_customer: Home gardeners buying a connected soil sensor and water valve, later farmers
problem: Gardeners cannot tell when and how much to water; Edyn sold a solar powered sensor and app that measures soil moisture and temperature and advises or automates care.
business_model: Hardware sale through Kickstarter and retail plus app

founders.name: Jason Aramburu
founders.background_notes: Soil scientist who worked with hundreds of Kenyan farmers to raise crop yields (TechCrunch).

competitors.name: Parrot Flower Power
competitors.what: Stick shaped Bluetooth plant sensor and phone app

competitors.name: Koubachi
competitors.what: Plant sensor and advice system with indoor and outdoor models

competitors.name: PlantLink
competitors.what: Kickstarter funded soil moisture sensor sending watering alerts

technical_complexity.rationale: Solar powered wireless soil sensor with cloud analytics, a water valve attachment and industrial design from Fuseproject, all needing hardware manufacturing at small scale.

defensibility.rationale: Rivals Flower Power, Koubachi and PlantLink already sold sensors; Edyn claimed automated care and recommendations as its difference and had strong industrial design.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Edyn; customer reviews on a retailer site (anecdotal) say the apps and website later stopped working.

market_need_then: Smart home and IoT interest in 2014, a Kickstarter that passed its 100,000 dollar goal, and later Home Depot distribution (TechCrunch headline) indicate consumer interest in connected gardening.

branding.name_origin: Per a quote from Yves Behar in a Dexigner article seen only in search results, the name came from the concept of a utopian garden; unverified from an opened page.
branding.domain_note: Used edyn.com (exact name .com); it did not resolve from the research environment in 2026.

identity.visual_style: Designed by Yves Behar's Fuseproject, which IDSA credits for the overall brand identity and the first product

rebrands.why: Relaunched under a new name with the Kickstarter production run (TechCrunch); reason not given

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in TechCrunch, Modern Farmer, Metropolis and Harvard D3; Soil IQ was a TechCrunch Disrupt finalist.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong design press and a designer led identity, but no sources show a community or repeat purchase driven by the brand.

pivots.to: Precision agriculture hardware rollout alongside consumer product
pivots.why: AgFunder headline describes the 2016 seed as funding a precision ag hardware rollout; no company statement read

outcome_analysis: Edyn went from Soil IQ to a Fuseproject branded Kickstarter product in mid 2014, raised about 2.9M by 2016 per aggregators, and reached retail distribution, but no source states when or why it stopped. Customer reviews say the apps and site went dead and the YC page lists it Inactive, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: Exit type unknown because the status is Inactive but no announcement of a shutdown or acquisition was found; edyn.com could not be fetched (host did not resolve in this session). Funding conflicts: CB Insights labels a 2015 Series A and a 2016 Series A-II with 4.24M total over 11 rounds, while press calls the 2016 round a 2M seed and Village and BounceWatch give 2.85M to 2.9M totals; the stage labels follow the press. The 2015 seed of 2.075M comes from an AgFunder summary of an earlier raise and may overlap the 1M angel money reported by TechCrunch in June 2014. Yves Behar worked with the company from the start but no source read calls him a co-founder, so he is not listed. A claim that Google bought the company was a mix up with Nest and was ignored. Competitor sources were opened only through search summaries.
